## Problem
Discovered during an early draft of the sibling "rank aggregation by priority" ticket
(beaming-snively-urial): `src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py:13,137` imports `_severity_rank` from
`aggregate.py` directly and sorts its own findings list by it
(`findings.sort(key=_severity_rank, reverse=True)`). `spec_scan.py`'s findings come straight
from the "spec-alignment" LLM reviewer's structured output via `finalize_findings`
(`findings.py`) -- they never pass through `pass3_decide` and never get `priority`.

## OBSOLETED
This ticket's premise no longer holds, for two independent reasons, both confirmed against
the ACTUAL, FINAL, landed state of the tickets named below (not an early draft):

1. Ticket `beaming-snively-urial` was itself corrected mid-implementation after research
   showed `aggregate.py::aggregate_findings`/`_severity_rank` is dead code (no caller in
   `src/rebar/` since ADR 0075). Its FINAL, closed scope explicitly excludes `aggregate.py`
   -- its acceptance criteria required (and its landed change satisfies)
   `git diff --stat src/rebar/llm/aggregate.py` being EMPTY. `_severity_rank`/`_SEVERITY_RANK`
   in `aggregate.py` are therefore completely untouched by this epic, in perpetuity as far as
   this epic's scope goes -- there is no migration for `spec_scan.py`'s import of them to be
   broken BY.
2. Separately, `findings.py`'s shared `SEVERITIES`/`normalize_finding`/`Finding.severity`
   vocabulary (which `spec_scan.py`'s findings are normalized through, independent of
   `_severity_rank`) is ALSO staying intact per the epic's corrected architecture: it serves a
   completion-verification module cluster (`completion_reconcile.py`, `completion_child_gate.py`,
   `epic_bug_screen.py`, `workflow/gate_ops.py`, `workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py`) that
   hardcodes `severity` as its ONLY signal with no priority/decision/impact alternative --
   deleting it would break that cluster with no fallback. Only the review-kernel
   (`pass3_decide`) stops stamping `severity` onto ITS OWN emitted findings; nothing else in
   `findings.py` changes.

The epic's own AC-3 ("every finding ... carries priority/decision") is being corrected
separately (on the still-open epic ticket) to scope that claim to review-kernel/DET-tier
findings specifically, not universally to every finding any reviewer anywhere produces --
`spec_scan.py`'s findings were never in that scope.

## Approach (superseded, retained for context only -- not implemented)
Would have mapped spec_scan's severity string to a numeric priority via a fixed ordinal
mapping (any unrecognized/missing severity defaulting to 0.0) before sorting by priority
instead of `_severity_rank`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Confirmed against the FINAL, closed state of `beaming-snively-urial` (zero diff to
  `aggregate.py`) and the epic's corrected architecture (findings.py's severity vocabulary
  stays intact) that `spec_scan.py` requires no change.

## Testing
Not applicable -- no code change made.
